c.tagline: Where the Silk Road meets snow-capped Tian Shan peaks.

taxi.fareNote: Most rides are booked via Yandex Go or inDrive with fixed upfront pricing; hailed street taxis should have a fare agreed before departure.

emergency.note: Fire is 101; the unified emergency number 112 also connects to all services.

hood_landmark.Kok-Tobe / Bostandyk: Kok-Tobe Cable Car Lower Station, Almaty

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets around the Green Bazaar and on crowded buses, and skip unofficial street taxis late at night.

hood_desc: The historic heart of Almaty around Panfilov Park and Zenkov Cathedral, packed with museums, cafes and Soviet-era architecture; ideal for first-time visitors who want to walk everywhere.
The bustling commercial core near Republic Square and the Zhibek Zholy pedestrian street, with department stores, restaurants and nightlife; suits travelers who want energy and easy transit access.
A leafy, embassy-lined avenue of upscale malls, cafes and business hotels; good for business travelers and those wanting a quieter, polished base close to shopping.
Almaty's glossy modern financial district around Esentai Mall and Almaty Tower, with fine dining and designer boutiques; suits luxury travelers and business visitors.
A green, hillside area near the Kok-Tobe cable car and Central Stadium with mountain views; good for families and travelers who prefer a quieter, local vibe.
lodging: Best Western Plus Atakent Park Hotel

water.note: Treated but quality is inconsistent; bottled, boiled, or filtered water is recommended for visitors.

transit.pay: Fares on the metro, buses and BRT are paid with the contactless Onai smart card (tap to reload and ride) or by tapping a bank card/phone directly at the turnstile or validator; single-use paper tokens are also sold at metro stations. Cash is generally not accepted on board buses.
transit.hours: Metro runs about 6:20am-midnight daily; most city buses operate roughly 6am-11pm with a few late-night routes; taxis and ride-hailing apps run 24/7.
transit.note: The single metro line covers only part of the city, so buses and ride-hailing apps are essential for getting around.

airport.name: Almaty International Airport (ALA)
airport.drive: 20-30 min to city center in light traffic; up to 45-60 min during rush hour

tip.r: Not traditionally required, but rounding up or leaving 5-10% at restaurants is increasingly common and appreciated where no service charge is included.

places.name: Kishlak

places.name: Auyl

food.name: Plov
food.desc: Rice slow-cooked in a kazan with lamb, carrot, cumin and whole garlic until every grain is glossy. Served in mounds for sharing.

places.name: Alasha

places.name: Tarkhun National Cuisine

places.name: Kishlak

food.desc: Tandoor-baked meat pastries, puffy fried dough balls served with butter and jam, and kazy horse sausage sliced cold as a starter.

places.name: Green Bazaar (Zelyony Bazar)
places.note: Almaty's great market: tandoor samsa, kazy, dried fruit and cheese balls to taste.

places.name: Kishlak

places.name: Sandyq
places.note: Presents baursak, kazy and other steppe specialities in a modern format.

food.name: Kumys and shubat
food.desc: Fermented mare's milk (kumys) and camel milk (shubat): sour, fizzy, mildly alcoholic and central to Kazakh nomadic tradition.

places.name: Green Bazaar
places.note: Dairy row sells kumys and shubat by the bottle; vendors let you taste first.

places.name: Auyl

places.name: Sandyq
places.note: Good place for a first, gentler glass of kumys with dinner.

food.name: Kazakh milk tea and apple kompot
food.desc: Strong black tea poured with milk, cream and salt or sugar, refilled endlessly; plus kompot made from the Almaty region's famous apples.

places.name: Sandyq
places.note: Tea served in the traditional way with baursak and sweets.

places.name: Green Bazaar tea stalls

places.name: Alasha
places.note: Pots of tea and house kompot accompany every meal.

landmarks: Ascension (Zenkov) Cathedral
A vividly painted wooden Russian Orthodox cathedral in Panfilov Park, famed for being built entirely without nails.
Kok-Tobe Hill
A hilltop park reached by cable car offering panoramic views of Almaty against the backdrop of the Tian Shan mountains.
Medeu Skating Rink
The world's highest-altitude Olympic-size skating rink, set dramatically amid soaring mountain peaks.
Shymbulak Ski Resort
A premier mountain resort above the city offering sweeping alpine views year-round via cable car.
Panfilov Park & 28 Panfilov Guardsmen Memorial
A leafy park centered on a monumental Soviet-era war memorial honoring the city's WWII heroes.
Almaty Tower (Kok-Tobe TV Tower)
The city's tallest structure, a striking telecommunications tower that anchors views from Kok-Tobe hill.
Green Bazaar (Zelenyi Bazaar)
A colorful indoor market bursting with Central Asian spices, dried fruits, and local life.
Republic Square
Almaty's grand central plaza featuring the Independence Monument and surrounding Soviet-modernist architecture.
Central State Museum of Kazakhstan
An imposing museum with a golden dome, showcasing Kazakh history, nomadic culture, and archaeology.
Hotel Kazakhstan
A Soviet-era modernist tower from 1977 whose elliptical silhouette and golden crown made it the city's tallest building and an enduring symbol of Almaty.

train.note: All mainline trains use Almaty-2 station at the north end of downtown, with northbound services also calling at Almaty-1 out towards the airport. KTZ runs a sleeper to Tashkent on alternate days, about 16 hours via Taraz and Shymkent, and a direct sleeper to Novosibirsk in Russia on odd dates; for Moscow you normally change at Astana, Saratov or Petropavl rather than riding a single through train, so check what is actually selling before you plan around it. The Almaty-Urumqi service into China was cancelled during the pandemic and has still not resumed. Carry your passport for overnight border checks, and be aware the KTZ booking site bilet.railways.kz is mostly in Kazakh and Russian.

bus.note: International coaches and shared minibuses use Sayran bus station about 8 km west of the centre, and its own site ma-sairan.kz publishes the timetable and sells tickets online, which is unusual for the region. Bishkek is the busiest run at roughly 4-5 hours with five departures a day via the Korday border, Karakol takes about 8 hours, Tashkent about 14 hours twice daily, and early-morning buses cross to Yining (12 hr) and Urumqi (19 hr) in China. Most Western nationalities enter Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan visa-free, but China requires a visa arranged well in advance. The old Sayakhat terminal has been demolished, though intercity taxis and marshrutkas may still drop you at that junction rather than at Sayran.

ferry.note: Almaty is landlocked; there are no ferries. Kazakhstan's only international sea link is the Caspian ferry from Aktau in the far west to Baku, Azerbaijan.

half.name: Big Almaty Lake
half.blurb: Turquoise alpine lake ringed by snowy peaks in the Trans-Ili Alatau mountains.

half.name: Shymbulak and Medeu
half.blurb: High mountain ski resort and famous ice rink reached by scenic cable car.

half.name: Turgen Gorge
half.blurb: Forested gorge with tumbling waterfalls, hot springs and excellent hiking trails.

half.name: Issyk Lake
half.blurb: Serene mountain lake with vivid waters set among wooded slopes and peaks.

half.name: Tamgaly Tas
half.blurb: Riverside site of ancient Buddhist rock carvings above the Ili River.

full.name: Charyn Canyon
full.blurb: Dramatic red rock canyon often compared to a smaller Grand Canyon carved by rivers.
